title: Oral fluid intake in hospitalized patients and its relevance for nursing care. A randomized controlled trial of audiovisual drinking reminder at the center for neurology at the University Hospital Bonn
summary:
Drinking enough fluids regularly is an important part of a healthy diet. However, both in general and in hospitals, it has been observed that patients often do not drink enough fluids. This study examines the drinking behavior of patients using a smart drinking cup. Two groups are formed as part of the study, with one study group using a smart drinking cup that not only measures fluid intake but also has a drinking reminder system with a drinking quantity display.

The aim of the study is to investigate the influence of drinking memories on drinking behavior, to describe drinking behavior in the context of other factors, and to examine whether there are any correlations with care-sensitive outcomes (e.g., falls, need for care).

interventions.name: Intervention group: Fluid intake is recorded by a smart drinking cup. The drinking cup has an active drinking reminder system with a drinking volume display (60-minute reminder if the drinking target is not met; 7:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m.). The drinking targets are set at 1.6 liters/day for women and 2.
Control group: The amounts drunk are recorded by a smart drinking cup. There is no reminder to drink and no display of the amount drunk.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Proficiency in spoken and written German in order to understand the requirements of the study
- Presence of a neurological disease or suspected diagnosis
-    Expected hospital stay >3 days
-    Written consent to participate in the study
-    The patient is able to use the smart drinking cup
-    Hearing and vision enable perception of the environment
Exclusion criteria:
- Male or female subjects, age < 18 years
- Medically prescribed fluid restrictions
- Fasting during parenteral nutrition or enteral nutrition via feeding tube/PEG
- Relevant swallowing disorders that preclude unsupervised independent drinking
- Expected inpatient stay ≤3 days
- Lack of written consent to participate in the study
- Deafness/hearing impairment (without hearing aid)/blindness
- Infusion therapy >1500ml/day
